title: When the Ice Broke: New Climate Engagement Trends Exposed by the Nepal-Tibet Flash Flood - The China-Global South Project

Key Takeaways Climate impacts are reshaping bilateral ties, as the Nepal - China flash flood from unstable Himalayan glaciers exposed border vulnerabilities.

On August 26, 2026, a sudden collapse of ice and rock unleashed a catastrophic flash flood down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river valleys, devastating northern Nepal and spilling across the border into Tibet. Villages were wiped out, bridges and roads destroyed, and hydropower stations wrecked. The death toll was severe, and will likely rise further as many remain unaccounted.

The episode has thrust China’s climate impact response with the Global South into the spotlight as never before. It also crystallizes several trends that have been building for years.

The first is that climate change has outgrown its role as a purely multilateral diplomatic issue for China. It’s increasingly woven into bilateral relationships, especially with neighboring states. The Nepal border disaster, rooted in long-term warming and the resulting instability of Himalayan glaciers, is a stark case study in how climate impacts can directly affect a border relationship. A similar dynamic is unfolding in Southeast Asia, where a warming climate is intensifying flood and drought risk across the Mekong basin, pushing China and downstream nations toward closer coordination on disaster response, early warning, and water management.

Second, the disaster illustrates the need for a shift in how China delivers climate assistance overseas. Where China’s support once centered on hardware (such as solar panels, solar water heaters, solar streetlights), it has increasingly moved toward offering technology, expertise, and platforms. In recent years, China has become a significant supplier of early-warning systems internationally, pairing its satellite and forecasting capabilities with data gathered on the ground in partner countries to improve disaster prediction. The Nepal disaster has brought new urgency to accelerating this approach.

Third, the fallout reveals a delicate position China occupies in climate responsibilities vis-à-vis Global South countries. Nepal initially called for “climate compensation” from China, the US, and India, invoking the language of climate justice. This demand immediately drew outsized attention because China is simultaneously a major polluter, Nepal’s neighbor, and a self-considered developing country. By September 3, however, Nepal had quickly walked back the request, claiming, in a meeting between its Foreign Minister and China’s ambassador to Nepal, that it would instead pursue support through existing multilateral climate channels.

That reversal captures the interesting tension at play. As climate change becomes more entangled with China’s relationships with its developing country neighbors, questions of climate responsibility and compensation remain a highly sensitive topic. Beijing is undoubtedly very wary of any precedent tying its emitter status to direct compensation claims.

Taken together, the Nepal-China disaster may be a preview of things to come. As climate impacts grow more severe, they’re likely to become a permanent and expanding thread in China’s relations with Global South nations. This will certainly bring both new frictions and new cooperation opportunities.

केरऽ विदेशी जलवायु सहायता हार्डवेयर स॑ ल॑ क॑ तकनीक आरू विशेषज्ञता म॑ बदली रहलऽ छै, खास करी क॑ ओकरऽ उपग्रह आरू पूर्वानुमान पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली । एहि आपदा सं जिम्मेदारी पर संवेदनशील तनाव के उजागर भेल : नेपाल के जलवायु मुआवजा के संक्षिप्त आह्वान जलवायु न्याय पर विवाद के उजागर केलक .

26 अगस्त 2026 क॑ अचानक बर्फ आरू चट्टान केरऽ ढहला स॑ भोटे कोशी आरू त्रिशुली नदी केरऽ घाटी के नीचें भयावह फ्लैश फ्लड पैदा होय गेलै, जेकरा स॑ उत्तरी नेपाल क॑ तबाह करी देलऽ गेलै आरू सीमा पार करी क॑ तिब्बत म॑ फैललऽ गेलै । गाम-गाम सफाया भ गेल, पुल आ सड़क तबाह भ गेल, आ जलविद्युत स्टेशन ध्वस्त भ गेल। मृतक केरऽ संख्या गंभीर छेलै, आरू संभव छै कि आरू बढ़ी जैतै, कैन्हेंकि बहुत लोगऽ के हिसाब-किताब नै छै ।

ई एपिसोड न॑ चीन केरऽ ग्लोबल साउथ के साथ जलवायु प्रभाव प्रतिक्रिया क॑ ऐन्हऽ तरह स॑ चर्चा म॑ लानल॑ छै जेतना कि पहलऽ कहियो नै छेलै । ई कतेको एहन प्रवृत्ति के सेहो क्रिस्टलीकृत करैत अछि जे सालों स बनैत आबि रहल अछि।

पहिल ई छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन चीन लेली विशुद्ध बहुपक्षीय कूटनीतिक मुद्दा के रूप म॑ अपनऽ भूमिका स॑ आगू बढ़ी गेलऽ छै । ई तेजी स॑ द्विपक्षीय संबंधऽ म॑ बुनलऽ छै, खास करी क॑ पड़ोसी राज्यऽ के साथ । दीर्घकालीन गर्मी आरू एकरऽ परिणामस्वरूप हिमालयी ग्लेशियर केरऽ अस्थिरता म॑ जड़ जमाय वाला नेपाल सीमा आपदा ई बात केरऽ एगो शुद्ध केस स्टडी छै कि जलवायु केरऽ प्रभाव सीमा संबंध क॑ कोना सीधा प्रभावित करी सकै छै । दक्षिण पूर्व एशिया म॑ भी ऐसनऽ ही गतिशीलता खुली रहलऽ छै, जहां गर्म होय रहलऽ जलवायु के कारण पूरा मेकांग बेसिन म॑ बाढ़ आरू सूखा के खतरा तेज होय रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ चीन आरू नीचे के राष्ट्रऽ क॑ आपदा प्रतिक्रिया, पूर्व चेतावनी आरू जल प्रबंधन प॑ करीबी समन्वय के तरफ धकेललऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

दोसर, ई आपदा चीन विदेशऽ म॑ जलवायु सहायता केना पहुँचै छै, एकरा म॑ बदलाव के जरूरत क॑ दर्शाबै छै । जहाँ चीन केरऽ समर्थन कहियो हार्डवेयर (जैना कि सोलर पैनल, सोलर वॉटर हीटर, सोलर स्ट्रीटलाइट) प॑ केंद्रित छेलै, वहीं चीन केरऽ तेजी स॑ तकनीक, विशेषज्ञता, आरू प्लेटफॉर्म पेश करै के तरफ बढ़ी गेलऽ छै । हाल के सालऽ म॑ चीन अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर प॑ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली केरऽ एगो महत्वपूर्ण आपूर्तिकर्ता बनी गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ आपदा के भविष्यवाणी म॑ सुधार लेली अपनऽ उपग्रह आरू पूर्वानुमान क्षमता क॑ साझेदार देशऽ म॑ जमीन प॑ एकत्रित करलऽ गेलऽ आंकड़ऽ के साथ जोड़लऽ गेलऽ छै । नेपाल आपदा एहि दृष्टिकोण केँ तेज करबाक नव तात्कालिकता अनलक अछि ।

तेसरऽ, एकरऽ परिणाम स॑ पता चलै छै कि चीन केरऽ जलवायु जिम्मेदारी म॑ ग्लोबल साउथ देशऽ के सामने एगो नाजुक स्थिति छै । नेपाल शुरू मे जलवायु न्याय के भाषा के आह्वान करैत चीन, अमेरिका, आ भारत स “जलवायु मुआवजा” के आह्वान केलक । ई मांग तुरंत आउटसाइज के ध्यान आकर्षित करलकै, कैन्हेंकि चीन एक साथ एगो प्रमुख प्रदूषक, नेपाल के पड़ोसी, आरू एक स्वंगणित विकासशील देश छै । लेकिन ३ सितम्बर तलक नेपाल न॑ जल्दी स॑ ई आग्रह क॑ वापस करी क॑ अपनऽ विदेश मंत्री आरू नेपाल म॑ चीन केरऽ राजदूत के बीच एगो बैठक म॑ दावा करलकै कि वू एकरऽ बदला म॑ मौजूदा बहुपक्षीय जलवायु चैनलऽ के माध्यम स॑ समर्थन के पीछा करतै ।

ओ उलटफेर खेल मे रोचक तनाव केँ पकड़ि लैत अछि । जेना-जेना जलवायु परिवर्तन चीन केरऽ अपनऽ विकासशील देशऽ के पड़ोसी देशऽ के साथ संबंधऽ स॑ उलझलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, जलवायु जिम्मेदारी आरू मुआवजा के सवाल एगो बेहद संवेदनशील विषय बनलऽ छै । निस्संदेह बीजिंग अपनऽ एमिटर केरऽ दर्जा क॑ सीधा मुआवजा के दावा स॑ जोड़ै वाला कोनो भी मिसाल स॑ बहुत सावधान छै ।

एकरा मिला कए नेपाल-चीन आपदा आबै बला चीजक पूर्वावलोकन भ सकैत अछि । जेना-जेना जलवायु केरऽ प्रभाव बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, संभावना छै कि ई ग्लोबल साउथ राष्ट्रऽ के साथ चीन केरऽ संबंधऽ म॑ एगो स्थायी आरू विस्तारित धागा बनी जैतै । एहि स निश्चित रूप स नव घर्षण आ नव सहयोग क अवसर दुनू भेटत।

The recent floods in Nepal have raised fresh questions about China’s construction activity in Tibet. Mr Tsewang Dorji, Research Fellow at the Tibet Policy Institute, pointed out on the Gist that China has expanded roads, railways, airports and military infrastructure across Tibet, including in ecologically fragile areas close to India, Nepal and Bhutan.

He argues that Chinese infrastructure requires changing the patterns of nature, such as building railways by cutting mountains and creating dams on rivers. “Besides, China has also censored all the news and information and produced its own narrative around the recent flood, pointing towards how the situation in Nepal and Tibet is not a natural disaster.”

Dr Y Nithiyanandam, head of the Geospatial program at the Takshashila Institution, drew a more careful comparison between the construction and the latest disaster. He said that 3D assessment points to a glacial and slope failure that sent a mass of ice and debris into the valley. While the primary assessment points out that the natural disaster could be due to climate change, he cautions that much longer observation is required before attributing it to just nature.

He further adds that satellite imagery and remote sensing can only show where terrain is shifting and where new construction is appearing. However, it cannot be predicted precisely when a slope will give way. Nithiyanandam said that kind of assessment needs long-term ground monitoring alongside observations from space — difficult when access inside Tibet is restricted.

The restricted access also acts a blind spot in several other infrastructure projects created by China that may impact its neighbours, India included. The Medog dam is one of them.

Dorji highlights that China is building its giant hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo, in a vulnerable terrain exposed to earthquakes and landslides. Beijing continues to press ahead despite repeated environmental warnings. He adds that such development in Tibet will impact India’s environmental ecosystem too as the Himalayas are the lungs of India. However, Dorji adds, for China, “destruction is nothing,” following Mao’s and the Chinese Communist Party’s political slogan that ‘man must conquer nature’.

Dr Nithiyanandam adds that the dam can lead to changes in snowfall, surface water and river behaviour across the Tibetan Plateau. Upstream alterations can pose further risks to downstream ecosystems and livelihoods, long before their cause becomes easy to establish or ends up getting attributed to ‘climate change’.

While India can watch much of this construction in Tibet from space, the next concern for New Delhi is how to manage these changes in the Himalayas when they pose this level of risk to life and property. Although both experts warn that local voices remain unheard, they point out that the ecological aspect needs to be measured.

नेपाल मे हाल मे आयल बाढ़ि मे चीन के तिब्बत मे निर्माण गतिविधि पर नव सवाल उठल अछि. तिब्बत नीति संस्थान केरऽ रिसर्च फेलो श्री त्सेवांग दोरजी न॑ गिस्ट प॑ ई बात के ओर इशारा करलकै कि चीन न॑ पूरा तिब्बत म॑ सड़क, रेलवे, हवाई अड्डा आरू सैन्य बुनियादी ढाँचा के विस्तार करलकै, जेकरा म॑ भारत, नेपाल आरू भूटान के नजदीक पारिस्थितिकी के दृष्टि स॑ नाजुक क्षेत्र भी शामिल छै ।

हुनकऽ तर्क छै कि चीनी बुनियादी ढाँचा म॑ प्रकृति केरऽ पैटर्न म॑ बदलाव करै के जरूरत छै, जेना कि पहाड़ क॑ काटी क॑ रेलवे बनाबै आरू नदी प॑ बांध बनाबै के जरूरत छै । “एकरऽ अलावा चीन न॑ भी सब खबर आरू जानकारी क॑ सेंसर करी क॑ हाल केरऽ बाढ़ के आसपास अपनऽ कथ्य तैयार करी क॑ ई तरफ इशारा करी क॑ कि नेपाल आरू तिब्बत केरऽ स्थिति कोना प्राकृतिक आपदा नै छै ।”

तक्षशिला संस्थान केरऽ भू-स्थानिक कार्यक्रम केरऽ प्रमुख डॉ. वाई निथियानंदम न॑ निर्माण आरू नवीनतम आपदा के बीच अधिक सावधानीपूर्वक तुलना करलकै । हुनी कहलकै कि 3D आकलन हिमनदी आरू ढलान के विफलता के तरफ इशारा करै छै जेकरा स॑ बर्फ आरू मलबा के द्रव्यमान घाटी म॑ भेजलऽ गेलै । प्राथमिक आकलन म॑ जहाँ ई बात के ओर इशारा करलऽ गेलऽ छै कि प्राकृतिक आपदा जलवायु परिवर्तन के वजह स॑ भी होय सकै छै, वहीं हुनी चेतावनी दै छै कि एकरा न्यायसंगत प्रकृति के कारण बताबै स॑ पहल॑ एकरा लेली बहुत लम्बा समय तलक अवलोकन के जरूरत छै ।

हुनी आरू कहै छै कि उपग्रह इमेजरी आरू रिमोट सेंसिंग स॑ खाली ई पता चल॑ सकै छै कि इलाका कहाँ शिफ्ट होय रहलऽ छै आरू कत॑ नया निर्माण दिखाय रहलऽ छै । मुदा, कोनो ढलान कहिया रास्ता देत से ठीक-ठीक अनुमान नहिं लगाओल जा सकैत अछि. निथियानंदम न॑ कहलकै कि ई तरह के आकलन लेली अंतरिक्ष स॑ अवलोकन के साथ-साथ दीर्घकालिक जमीनी निगरानी के जरूरत छै — जब॑ तिब्बत के भीतर पहुँच प्रतिबंधित होय जाय छै त॑ मुश्किल छै ।

प्रतिबंधित पहुँच चीन द्वारा बनाओल गेल कईटा अन्य बुनियादी ढांचा परियोजना मे सेहो अंधापन क काज करैत अछि जे भारत सहित ओकर पड़ोसी देश कए प्रभावित क सकैत अछि । मेडोग बांध सेहो ओहि मे स एक अछि।

दोरजी ई बात प॑ प्रकाश डालै छै कि चीन अपनऽ विशाल जलविद्युत परियोजना यारलुंग त्सांगपो प॑ बनाबै छै, जे भूकंप आरू भूस्खलन के सामना करै वाला कमजोर इलाका म॑ छै । बेर-बेर पर्यावरण के चेतावनी के बावजूद बीजिंग आगू बढ़ैत अछि. हुनी आरू कहै छै कि तिब्बत मँ ऐसनौ विकास स॑ भारत केरऽ पर्यावरण पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र प॑ भी असर पड़तै, कैन्हेंकि हिमालय भारत केरऽ फेफड़ा छेकै । लेकिन, डोर्जी आरू कहै छै, चीन लेली, “विनाश कुछ भी नै छै,” माओ आरू चीनी कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी केरऽ राजनीतिक नारा के पालन करतें हुअ॑ कि ‘मनुष्य क॑ प्रकृति प॑ जीत हासिल करना चाहियऽ’ ।

डॉ. निथियानंदम आरू कहै छै कि ई बांध स॑ तिब्बती पठार भर म॑ बर्फबारी, सतही पानी आरू नदी के व्यवहार म॑ बदलाव आबी सकै छै । अपस्ट्रीम परिवर्तन डाउनस्ट्रीम पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र आ आजीविका कें लेल आ बेसि जोखिम पैदा कयर सकय छै, बहुत पहिले ओकर कारण कें स्थापित करनाय आसान भ जायत छै या अंत मे ‘जलवायु परिवर्तन’ कें जिम्मेदार ठहराएल जायत छै.

भारत तिब्बत केरऽ ई निर्माण केरऽ बहुत हिस्सा अंतरिक्ष स॑ देख॑ सकै छै, लेकिन नई दिल्ली लेली अगला चिंता ई छै कि जब॑ ई बदलाव जीवन आरू संपत्ति लेली ई स्तर के खतरा पैदा करै छै त॑ हिमालय म॑ ई बदलाव क॑ कोना प्रबंधित करलऽ जाय । हालांकि दुनू विशेषज्ञ चेतावनी दैत छथि जे स्थानीय आवाज अनसुना रहैत अछि, मुदा ओ इ बतबैत छथि जे पारिस्थितिकी पहलू कए मापबाक जरूरत अछि।

full_article:
The August 26 flash floods on the Nepal-China border wiped out or badly damaged 281 MW of installed capacity and 388 MW under construction in Nepal, with significant financial losses.

Some experts argue the flood should prompt Nepal to prioritise domestic consumption over its export-driven hydropower strategy, citing both physical disaster risk and falling prices of electricity in India even as the flood pushes up the cost of generation in Nepal.

Nepal had aimed to export more electricity than it consumes domestically and narrow its trade deficit with India by 2035.

The disaster threatens Nepal’s newly achieved net-exporter status heading into winter’s low-flow season, and is accelerating calls to scale up solar power. See All Key Ideas

Nepal’s long-held policy of harnessing hydroelectricity and using it for economic growth has met new challenges: potential catastrophic floods in the snow-fed rivers amid rising global temperatures.

The August 26 floods that originated on the Nepal-China border, and that knocked out around 10% of installed power from the national grid, has prompted a debate on whether Nepal should rethink its overall hydropower strategy or just adopt better-engineered plants. Amid this, the flood could jeopardise the country’s clean energy targets and push it to adopt more solar power.

Immediate impacts

The recent flash flood crippled a combined installed generation capacity of 281 megawatts, including a solar power plant, and damaged four other under-construction projects, totaling a capacity of 700 MW. One of the oldest hydroelectric plants, the 14.1-MW Devighat Hydroelectric Plant, commissioned 42 years ago, was wiped out. Further downstream, the flood badly damaged a 25-MW solar power plant, according to data compiled by Mongabay from official sources. Similarly, with a hub of a transmission line washed away on the Trishuli river’s banks, another 150 MW of power from different power plants is cut off from the national grid system.

Transmission lines, including a substation on the Trishuli riverbank, were also destroyed. While officials are assessing the damage, estimates put losses at hundreds of billions of Nepali rupees, according to media reports. They say they can’t yet provide timelines for when the affected projects will resume generation.

Around 983 engineers and workers are feared trapped inside the tunnels or power houses and they are listed as people out of contact in the government records, according to the latest press release issued by Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal (IPPAN) on September 1. But the government records have counted only 639 missing people from the hydropower projects.

A drone view shows a major section of Pasang Lhamu highway washed away along swollen Trishuli river by recent flash floods. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh)

The exception: Super Trishuli

Not every project in the basin was swept away. The 100-MW Super Trishuli Hydropower Project endured the flood without major impact, even as the flood washed away several bridges upstream. The project sits about 100 kilometres downstream of Betrawati Bazar, one of the hardest-hit towns along the river.

For those skeptical that, due to the floods, Nepal requires to reconsider its export ambitions rather than just its engineering standards, Super Trishuli offers clues to make hydropower plants resilient within the existing hydropower-for-export model, not a reason to abandon it. In a Facebook post, project surveyor Laxman Devkota pointed to several design factors behind its survival: the project’s location away from the river, and the flood-probability assessment carried out before construction.

The state-owned power utility, for its part, has struck a notably calmer tone than some of the policy voices below. The Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) says supply was restored in most affected areas within two days and has assured households nationwide that supply remains adequate despite the damage elsewhere. Mongabay reached out to the NEA for comments on long-term impacts of the flood on the power sector. They didn’t respond to the query, saying that their priority now was to rescue those trapped inside the tunnels of hydropower projects.

Trishuli Hydropower Plant in 2016. Image by Paani Program via Flickr (CC BY-ND 2.0).

Design lessons: Surface vs. underground

The flood exposed a clear pattern. The worst damage hit powerhouses built on the surface, and dams and desanders located on or near the riverbed. Newer plants with underground powerhouses and desanders held up comparatively well.

Kulman Ghising, who headed Nepal’s electricity utility for about eight years and later served as the energy minister, called the flood a once-in-a-century event that nonetheless carries major lessons for project design and site regulation. “We need to design the plants resilient to floods and, most importantly, adopt early warning systems as well as robust emergency evacuation measures, and make longer access tunnels to the powerhouse to save it from floodwater,” he said.

Shailendra Guragain, former president of the IPPAN, echoed the point, saying that surface-built powerhouses and dams were wiped out or damaged, while underground construction paired with emergency rescue planning could help future projects withstand similar floods. He noted that these surface structures were originally built with cost, not resilience, in mind.

In an article in Nepal’s Spotlight magazine, Mohan Das Manandhar, chair of the Nepal Energy Foundation (NEF), framed the lesson this way: Hydropower projects shouldn’t just be built “away from the river,” but designed around the possibility that the river can become extraordinarily destructive. Current project designs rely on just 20 to 30 years of water discharge data, according to the Department of Electricity Development. Manandhar argued that critical infrastructure along snow-fed rivers should be approved only after assessing maximum credible floods, debris flows and cascading hazards. Both Manandhar and Bibek Kandel, advisor to the minister for energy, water resources and irrigation, estimate such design changes would raise minimum project costs by 10 to 12%.

Kaligandaki hydropower dam. Image by Krish Dulal via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0).

Policy rethink: Is export-driven hydropower still viable?

Shree Raj Shakya, head of the center for energy studies at Tribhuvan University’s Institute of Engineering in Lalitpur, said the increased risk to hydropower on snow-fed rivers should prompt Nepal to reconsider its policy of generating and exporting hydroelectricity. “The need of the hour is to put the strategy of electricity for domestic consumption in a more pragmatic way rather than aiming to export it, because there is no alternative to the generation of hydroelectricity in the country amid rising prices of fossil fuel,” he said. He warned the damage could reduce power supply this coming winter and delay Nepal’s clean energy transition plans through 2030 and 2035. According to Nepal’s Long-term Strategy for Net-zero Emissions, the country will need 14,300 MW of electricity under an additional-measures scenario by 2030.

Shakya argued export-focused strategy carries a double risk: The physical risk of disasters — like this one — and a market risk, since electricity prices have fallen sharply in neighboring India even as the flood pushes up the cost of generation at home.

With a technically and economically feasible capacity of 43,000 MW, Nepal has aimed to export more electricity than it consumes domestically and narrow its trade deficit with India by 2035 — targeting 15,000 MW of hydroelectricity exports on top of 13,500 MW for domestic consumption, according to the Energy Development Roadmap, 2025. Notably, as of this writing, the government has not revised or walked back these targets in response to the flood. Nepal’s energy transition goals also include electrifying 25% of household kitchens and converting 30% of industrial boilers to electric power by 2030, making 90% of new passenger vehicles electric by 2030, and converting 100% of iron and steel furnaces to electricity-powered ones by 2035.

Manandhar, of NEF, took a more measured view than Shakya. Export, he argued, remains essential for balancing seasonal supply-demand gaps, and domestic consumption should simply be prioritised within that model, not instead of it. He also said he fears the scale of loss of life in the flood could discourage clean-energy adoption and push some consumers back toward fossil fuels.

The question is not limited to a single hydropower project and its safety, but to consider each river basin, said Arjun Dhakal, environment and climate change economist. Dhakal has been publicly expressing concern over the unplanned proliferation of hydropower in the Trishuli region. More than 30 projects are either in operation or under construction in the river basin. “The scale of damages, particularly on hydropower projects occurred, because of haphazard permissions to build hydropower projects in the river basin without considering the possible natural risks including glacial lake outburst flood originating from Tibet,” he told Mongabay. He said that the government should prepare basin-level plans to designate where power plants should be located.

An electrical equipment at a power plant is partially buried in slush brought in by the Trishuli river in flash floods, in Dhading district, August 30, 2026. (AP Photo/Niranjan Shrestha)

Economic fallout

The flash flood is set to make electricity costlier by at least 10-12%, according to hydropower engineers and energy experts. Kandel said Nepal can no longer rely on low-cost engineering: “We need to work on strengthening all kinds of infrastructure we are making, including hydropower projects, to withstand disasters like the recent flood.”

Ram Prasad Dhital, chairman of the Electricity Regulatory Commission (ERC), said developers will have to build stronger infrastructure, with the added cost ultimately passed on to consumers: “It’s obvious that someone has to pay for it.” Dhital has proposed a loss-and-damage fund specifically for hydropower projects to help pay for recovery from this flood and future damage elsewhere. The added generation cost comes on top of a 5% value-added tax on household electricity consumers, which has been in effect since mid-July.

The timing compounds the pain. In the fiscal year ending mid-July, Nepal achieved net-exporter status for the first time in nearly a decade of electricity trade with India, netting 18.75 billion rupees (roughly $142 million) from sales to India and Bangladesh, according to the NEA report for 2026.

That status is now at risk: while the damage hasn’t yet significantly affected supply and Nepal is currently in its surplus generation season, the picture changes in winter, when flow in snow-fed rivers dwindles just as demand peaks. The country will likely need to import more electricity from India to meet peak winter demand, reversing last year’s export gain.

Aftermath of flash flooding at the confluence of the Trishuli and Tadi rivers in the Devighat area of Nuwakot district. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh)

Solar opportunity

The flood has opened space to promote the less risky solar power as part of the energy mix. Solar currently makes up less than 3% of Nepal’s total electricity generation, according to government data.

A total of 12 solar projects with a combined capacity of 89 MW are already under installation stages and 83 projects of varying capacities are under preliminary study, according to government licensing data.

Shakya suggested solar power contribution could be scaled to as much as 20%, citing falling installation costs and advances in battery storage: “The cost of solar installations is cheaper today, and technological advancement of battery storage may also provide an opportunity for promoting it up to 20%.” During winter, when river flow drops, solar could compensate for demand during daylight hours and preserve hydropower reserves for peak morning and evening loads, he said.

Banner image: People stand on remnants of a bridge which spanned across Trishuli river and was washed away in flash floods, in Dhading district. (AP Photo/Niranjan Shrestha)

नीति पर पुनर्विचार : की निर्यात संचालित जलविद्युत एखनो व्यवहार्य अछि?

ललितपुर स्थित त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय के अभियांत्रिकी संस्थान के ऊर्जा अध्ययन केंद्र के प्रमुख श्री राज शाक्य कहलनि जे, बर्फ सं चलय वाला नदी पर जलविद्युत के बढ़ल जोखिम के कारण नेपाल के जलविद्युत उत्पादन आ निर्यात के नीति पर पुनर्विचार करबाक चाही। ओ कहला जे एहि घंटा क जरूरत अछि जे घरेलू खपत लेल बिजली क रणनीति कए निर्यात करबाक लक्ष्य स बेसी व्यावहारिक तरीका स राखल जाए, किया कि जीवाश्म ईंधन क बढ़ैत दाम क बीच देश मे जलविद्युत उत्पादन क कोनो विकल्प नहि अछि। ओ चेतावनी देलनि जे एहि आगामी जाड़ मे एहि नुकसान स बिजली आपूर्ति मे कमी आबि सकैत अछि आ नेपाल क स्वच्छ ऊर्जा संक्रमण योजना मे 2030 आ 2035 तक देरी भ सकैत अछि।नेपाल क शुद्ध शून्य उत्सर्जन क दीर्घकालीन रणनीति क अनुसार 2030 तक देश कए अतिरिक्त उपाय क परिदृश्य क तहत 14,300 मेगावाट बिजली क जरूरत पड़त।

शाक्य केरऽ तर्क छेलै कि निर्यात केंद्रित रणनीति म॑ दोगुना जोखिम छै : आपदा केरऽ भौतिक जोखिम — जेना कि ई — आरू बाजार केरऽ जोखिम, कैन्हेंकि पड़ोसी देश भारत म॑ बिजली केरऽ दाम म॑ भारी गिरावट आबी गेलऽ छै, भले ही बाढ़ स॑ घरऽ म॑ उत्पादन केरऽ लागत बढ़ी जाय छै ।

43,000 मेगावाट के तकनीकी आरू आर्थिक रूप स॑ व्यवहार्य क्षमता के साथ नेपाल न॑ घरेलू खपत स॑ अधिक बिजली निर्यात करै के लक्ष्य रखन॑ छै आरू 2035 तलक भारत के साथ अपनऽ व्यापार घाटा क॑ कम करै के लक्ष्य रखन॑ छै — ऊर्जा विकास रोडमैप, 2025 के अनुसार घरेलू खपत लेली 13,500 मेगावाट के ऊपर 15,000 मेगावाट जलविद्युत निर्यात के लक्ष्य रखन॑ छै । उल्लेखनीय छै कि ई खबर लिखै के समय तक सरकार न॑ बाढ़ के जवाब म॑ ई लक्ष्यऽ म॑ संशोधन या वॉक बैक नै करलकै । नेपाल के ऊर्जा संक्रमण के लक्ष्य में 2030 तक 25% घर के रसोईघर के विद्युतीकरण आ 30% औद्योगिक बॉयलर के विद्युत शक्ति में बदलब, 2030 तक 90% नव यात्री वाहन के बिजली बनाबय के, आ 2035 तक 100% लोहा आ स्टील के भट्ठी के बिजली संचालित भट्ठी में बदलब सेहो शामिल अछि.

एनईएफ के मानन्धर शाक्य स बेसी नापल-जोखल दृष्टिकोण रखलनि। हुनकऽ तर्क छेलै कि मौसमी आपूर्ति-मांग के अंतर के संतुलन बनाबै लेली निर्यात जरूरी बनलऽ छै, आरू घरेलू खपत क॑ बस वू मॉडल के भीतर प्राथमिकता देना चाहियऽ, नै कि ओकरऽ जगह प॑ । हुनी ई भी कहलकै कि हुनका आशंका छै कि बाढ़ म॑ जान के नुकसान के पैमाना स्वच्छ ऊर्जा अपनाबै क॑ हतोत्साहित करी सकै छै आरू कुछ उपभोक्ता क॑ जीवाश्म ईंधन के तरफ वापस धकेल॑ सकै छै ।

पर्यावरण आरू जलवायु परिवर्तन अर्थशास्त्री अर्जुन ढकाल नँ कहलकै कि सवाल केवल एक जलविद्युत परियोजना आरू ओकरौ सुरक्षा तलक सीमित नै छै, बल्कि हर नदी बेसिन प विचार करै के छै । त्रिशूली क्षेत्र मे जलविद्युत के अनियोजित प्रसार के ल क धकाल सार्वजनिक रूप स चिंता व्यक्त करैत आबि रहल अछि। नदी बेसिन मे 30 स बेसी परियोजना या त संचालित अछि या निर्माणाधीन अछि। मोंगाबे स॑ कहलकै कि तिब्बत स॑ निकलै वाला हिमनदी झीलऽ म॑ फटै वाला बाढ़ सहित संभावित प्राकृतिक जोखिम प॑ विचार नै करी क॑ नदी बेसिन म॑ जलविद्युत परियोजना के निर्माण के बेतरतीब अनुमति के वजह स॑ नुकसान के पैमाना खास करी क॑ जलविद्युत परियोजना प॑ ऐलै । ओ कहला जे सरकार कए बेसिन स्तर क योजना तैयार करबाक चाही जाहि स इ निर्धारित कैल जाए जे बिजली संयंत्र कतय हेबाक चाही।

एकटा बिजली संयंत्र मे एकटा विद्युत उपकरण आंशिक रूप स त्रिशूली नदी द्वारा आनल गेल कीचड़ मे दफना देल गेल अछि, धड़िंग जिला मे, 30 अगस्त, 2026. (एपी फोटो/निरंजन श्रेष्ठ)

आर्थिक परिणाम

जलविद्युत इंजीनियर आ ऊर्जा विशेषज्ञ क अनुसार फ्लैश फ्लड स बिजली कम स कम 10-12% महग भ जाएत अछि। कंडेल कहलनि जे, नेपाल आब कम लागत वाला इंजीनियरिंग पर भरोसा नहि क सकैत अछि: “हमरा सब के हाल के बाढ़ि सन आपदा के सामना करय लेल जलविद्युत परियोजना सहित हम सब जे तरहक बुनियादी ढांचा बना रहल छी ओकरा मजबूत करय पर काज करय के जरूरत अछि।”

बिजली नियामक आयोग (ईआरसी) के अध्यक्ष रामप्रसाद धीतल न॑ कहलकै कि डेवलपर क॑ मजबूत बुनियादी ढाँचा बनाबै ल॑ पड़तै, जेकरा म॑ अतिरिक्त लागत अंततः उपभोक्ता क॑ पास करी देलऽ जैतै : “ई साफ छै कि एकरऽ भुगतान ककरो चुकाबै ल॑ पड़तै ।” धीतल न॑ विशेष रूप स॑ जलविद्युत परियोजना लेली नुकसान-क्षति कोष के प्रस्ताव रखन॑ छै, जेकरा स॑ ई बाढ़ आरू भविष्य म॑ अन्य जगहऽ प॑ होय वाला नुकसान स॑ वसूली के भुगतान म॑ मदद मिल॑ सक॑ । ई अतिरिक्त उत्पादन लागत घरेलू बिजली उपभोक्ता पर 5% मूल्य वर्धित कर के ऊपर आबै छै, जे जुलाई के मध्य स॑ लागू छै ।

समय दर्द के और बढ़ा दैत अछि। जुलाई के मध्य में समाप्त होबय वाला वित्तीय वर्ष में नेपाल भारत के साथ लगभग एक दशक के बिजली व्यापार में पहिल बेर शुद्ध निर्यातक के दर्जा प्राप्त केलक, जाहि में भारत आ बांग्लादेश के बिक्री सं 18.75 अरब रुपया (करीब 14.2 करोड़ डॉलर) के शुद्धि प्राप्त भेल, 2026 के एनईए रिपोर्ट के अनुसार.

ओ स्थिति आब खतरा मे अछि : जखन कि नुकसान के एखन धरि आपूर्ति पर कोनो खास असर नहिं पड़ल अछि आ नेपाल एखन अपन अधिशेष उत्पादन के मौसम मे अछि, जाड़ मे तस्वीर बदलैत अछि, जखन बर्फ सं भरल नदी मे बहाव ठीक ओहिना कम भ’ जाइत अछि जखन मांग चरम पर होइत अछि. संभव छै कि देश क॑ जाड़ा केरऽ पीक डिमांड क॑ पूरा करै लेली भारत स॑ अधिक बिजली आयात करै के जरूरत पड़तै, जेकरा स॑ पिछला साल केरऽ निर्यात लाभ क॑ उलट देलऽ जैतै ।

नुवाकोट जिला के देवीघाट क्षेत्र में त्रिशुली एवं ताडी नदी के संगम पर आकस्मिक बाढ़ के बाद | (एपी फोटो/राजेश कुमार सिंह)

सौर अवसर

बाढ़ि स॑ ऊर्जा मिश्रण के हिस्सा के रूप म॑ कम जोखिम वाला सौर ऊर्जा क॑ बढ़ावा दै लेली जगह खुललऽ छै । सरकारी आंकड़ा के अनुसार एखन नेपाल के कुल बिजली उत्पादन के 3% सं कम सौर ऊर्जा सं बनल अछि.

सरकारी लाइसेंसिंग के आंकड़ा के अनुसार 89 मेगावाट के संयुक्त क्षमता वाला कुल 12 सौर परियोजना पहिने सं स्थापना के चरण में अछि आओर अलग-अलग क्षमता के 83 परियोजना के प्रारंभिक अध्ययन के तहत अछि.

शाक्य न॑ सुझाव देलकै कि सौर ऊर्जा केरऽ योगदान क॑ २०% तलक बढ़ालऽ जाब॑ सकै छै, जेकरा म॑ इंस्टालेशन केरऽ लागत म॑ गिरावट आरू बैटरी स्टोरेज म॑ प्रगति के हवाला देलऽ गेलै: “आज सौर इंस्टालेशन केरऽ लागत सस्ता छै, आरू बैटरी स्टोरेज केरऽ तकनीकी उन्नति स॑ एकरा २०% तलक बढ़ावा दै के अवसर भी मिल॑ सकै छै ।” ओ कहला जे जाड़ क दौरान जखन नदी क बहाव कम भ जाइत अछि त सौर ऊर्जा दिन क उजाला क समय मांग क भरपाई क सकैत अछि आ भोर आ साँझ क पीक लोड क लेल जलविद्युत भंडार कए संरक्षित क सकैत अछि।

बैनर छवि : धडिंग जिला में, त्रिशुली नदी के पार फैलल आ झटका बाढ़ि में बहल पुल के अवशेष पर लोक ठाढ़ अछि. (एपी फोटो/निरंजन श्रेष्ठ)

ई कहानी मोंगाबे केरऽ ग्लोबल टीम न॑ रिपोर्ट करलकै आरू सबसें पहलऽ यहाँ हमरऽ मोंगाबे ग्लोबल साइट प॑ २ सितंबर २०२६ क॑ प्रकाशित करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

full_article:
© WFP/Shrawa Shrestha Food assistance reaches flood-affected families in Nuwakot district, Nepal.

This article is published in association with United Nations.

Nepal’s call for financial compensation following recent deadly floods underlines the need to help countries that contribute the least to climate change – but are increasingly grappling with its most lethal consequences, the top UN official in the country said on Wednesday.

Key points

1,367 people confirmed dead following the 26 August floods

5,132 people are still missing, including 587 foreign nationals, as search and rescue missions continue

13,646 people have been rescued

“The devastation Nepal has experienced is an extraordinary, stark illustration of the losses and damages that climate-vulnerable countries are increasingly facing,” UN Resident Coordinator for Nepal, Lila Pieters Yahia, told reporters by video link at UN Headquarters.

Nepal has contributed very little to global greenhouse gas emissions and yet is experiencing profound human and economic consequences from a changing climate, she explained from Kathmandu.

Triggered by a melting glacier, the 26 August floods affected about 84,270 Nepalis and resulted in vast destruction and damage to critical roads, schools, power grids and water systems across the Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading regions of northern Nepal.

Funds for climate-vulnerable

Nepal has approached the UN Loss and Damage Fund, established in 2022 to assist developing countries that are particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change.

“Nepal’s calls for climate justice speaks to a principle which lies at the heart of the international climate framework,” she said, noting that the country’s request is now being considered.

“Countries that are particularly vulnerable to climate change need adequate and accessible support to respond to loss and damages they did little to cause.”

Reaching those in need

Over the weekend, Ms. Yahia visited some of the worst affected areas, where floods had washed away whole settlements and entire riverbanks had shifted.

She met families continuing to search for relatives, adding that some had witnessed loved ones carried away by 20-metre-high waves.

At the same time, UN agencies and partners reported that aid has been reaching those most in need, however access to the most vulnerable remains a challenge, she said.

In a first during an emergency operation in Nepal, the World Food Programme (WFP) used cargo drones to deliver food to communities cut off by the floods.

Update on flash appeal

To meet those needs, the UN and the Government of Nepal launched a lifesaving flash appeal for $49.6 million on Friday to reach 84,000 people before the end of December, including with shelter, healthcare and cash support.

As of Wednesday, only $22 million has been received, Ms. Yahia said.

Urgent needs include restoring water systems, adding mobile clinics for pregnant women and providing mental healthcare to serve those affected by the disaster, she added.

ई लेख संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ के सहयोग स॑ प्रकाशित करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

हाल केरऽ घातक बाढ़ के बाद नेपाल केरऽ आर्थिक मुआवजा के आह्वान जलवायु परिवर्तन म॑ सबसें कम योगदान दै वाला देशऽ के मदद करै के जरूरत क॑ रेखांकित करै छै – लेकिन एकरऽ सबसें घातक परिणाम स॑ तेजी स॑ जूझै छै, ई बात क॑ देश म॑ संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ शीर्ष अधिकारी न॑ कहलकै ।

प्रमुख बिन्दु

26 अगस्त के बाढ़ि के बाद 1367 लोक के मौत के पुष्टि भेल अछि

खोज आ बचाव मिशन जारी रहला के कारण 587 विदेशी नागरिक सहित 5132 लोक एखनो लापता अछि

13,646 लोक के बचाओल गेल अछि

नेपाल के लेल संयुक्त राष्ट्र के निवासी समन्वयक लीला पीटर्स याहिया संयुक्त राष्ट्र मुख्यालय मे वीडियो लिंक के माध्यम सं पत्रकार सं बातचीत मे कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे जे तबाही भेल अछि ओ जलवायु सं कमजोर देश सब के जे नुकसान आ नुकसान के सामना करय पड़ि रहल अछि ओकर असाधारण, कड़ा उदाहरण अछि।

वैश्विक ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन मे नेपालक योगदान बहुत कम रहल अछि आ तइयो बदलैत जलवायु सँ गहींर मानवीय आ आर्थिक परिणामक अनुभव भ रहल अछि, काठमांडू सँ ओ बतौलनि ।

पिघलैत ग्लेशियर सँ शुरू भेल २६ अगस्तक बाढ़ि मे लगभग ८४,२७० नेपाली प्रभावित भेल आ एकर परिणामस्वरूप उत्तरी नेपालक रसुवा, नुवाकोट आ धडिंग क्षेत्र मे महत्वपूर्ण सड़क, स्कूल, बिजली ग्रिड आ जल प्रणालीक भारी तबाही आ क्षति भेल ।

जलवायु-असुरक्षित के लिये धन

नेपाल जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ प्रतिकूल प्रभाव स॑ विशेष रूप स॑ कमजोर विकासशील देशऽ के सहायता लेली २०२२ म॑ स्थापित संयुक्त राष्ट्र हानि आरू क्षति कोष स॑ संपर्क करलकै ।

देश केरऽ आग्रह प॑ अब॑ विचार करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, ई बात प॑ ध्यान दैत॑ हुअ॑ हुनी कहलकै कि नेपाल केरऽ जलवायु न्याय केरऽ आह्वान एगो ऐसनऽ सिद्धांत के बात करै छै जे अंतरराष्ट्रीय जलवायु ढाँचा के केंद्र म॑ छै ।

full_article:
In Langtang, Nepal, a group of locals and glaciologists gathered to mark the demise of the Yala glacier, which had shrunk by 66 per cent since the 1970s; its death—which for a glacier is marked when it no longer flows—was said to be imminent due to global warming. More than 50 people took the high-altitude trek to the site for a Buddhist ceremony and the placing of memorial plaques. This took place on 12th May 2025. Much worse was to come.

When a section of glacier cliff over half a kilometre wide sheared off the north face of the mountain of Langtang Lirung on 26th August this year, it fell 1,200 metres in a matter of seconds. As it hit the ground below, it registered as a magnitude 5.2 earthquake, and began a debris flow that travelled 100km down the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi river valleys at an average speed of 193km per hour, destroying towns, bridges and hydroelectricity dams in both Nepal and Tibet, China. Nepal’s early warning system relied on a network of river level-gauges that can register flash floods, but not 80m high mudflows and boulders the size of houses; many people had no time to get to safety. At the time of writing, 1,287 people are confirmed dead and more than 5,000 are still missing.

This was no freak event: like the smaller floods that hit communities in 2016, 2021 and 2024, it was caused in part by rapid warming. The Himalayan region as a whole is warming 50 per cent faster than the global average, and ice loss rates across the Hindu Kush have roughly doubled since 2000. A recent study of the Langtang region found it had warmed by 0.31°C every decade between 1960 and 2023. July was its second warmest July; August, up to the collapse, was the warmest ever.

Langtang Lirung’s high mountain slopes are held together by permafrost—and “As that frozen ground warms and ice inside thaws”, explains Umesh Haritashya, professor of earth, environment and sustainability at the University of Dayton, writing in the Conversation , the cement-like ground “weakens, and slopes that stood for thousands of years can lose their grip.” Meltwater from snow and ice seeps into cracks in the rock. Where it refreezes, cracks are prised ever wider. Satellite images of the site from before and after analysed by Dan Shugar at the University of Calgary show considerable snowmelt in the days preceding the disaster.

An editorial in the Nepali Times noted that that policymakers in the country had been warned “to prepare for floods unleashed by extreme weather, glacial lake outburst floods, and transboundary climate calamities”.

“This was not a ‘natural’ disaster,” it said. “Nothing about it was natural—not the glacier melting due to greenhouse gas buildup due to fossil fuel burning, not the location of expensive hydropower plants on trans-Himalayan rivers, not designing highways to follow rivers, not the settlements that have grown around them, not the corruption and greed, not the poor governance.” It was, in short, a predictable tragedy.

Perhaps predictably, too, the Nepal disaster has brought debates about “loss and damage” funding back to the fore. The concept of big emitters paying reparations to the countries that are most vulnerable to climate change had been front and centre at the Cop27 climate conference in Egypt in 2022—where a specific fund was established to help those hit by disasters—but it has since fallen out of favour. Compared to a stated need of $100bn-$580bn a year, the entire fund sits at $631m—towards which the UK (the fifth largest historical carbon emitter) has contributed $50m—with only around $350m available for reparations, and the rest going towards the costs of running the fund.

In 2025, while also cutting funds for overseas aid—including the disaster response team that might once have supported relief efforts in Nepal—the United States withdrew from the loss and damage fund agreement entirely. Other wealthy nations, including the UK, have also cut their international development aid obligations.

In the aftermath of the flood, Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal told Kantipur TV that, given Nepal’s own greenhouse-gas emissions were “practically negligible”, the country would be focusing less on talking about aid in future, and more on “justice and compensation”. The minister said: “This is not a matter of charity; it is a matter of legal and moral liability. The major industrial emitters—such as China, which is the world’s top emitter, the United States at number two, and India at number three—have a historical responsibility to compensate vulnerable nations like Nepal.”

Nepal had invested more than £6.7bn in building hydropower dams across the rivers, but August’s disaster flattened 12 hydroelectric plants, eradicating 10 per cent of the country’s total energy generation capacity. More than 20,000 houses will have to be rebuilt. The recovery costs are estimated by the government in Kathmandu to be more than $5bn, roughly 10 per cent of GDP. To cover these costs, Nepal still needs traditional aid—Khanal has put that figure at a relatively modest $20m.

Sunil Acharya wrote in the Guardian that “Loss and damage finance must… be additional to existing official development assistance”. I would add that it must also reach far higher figures than aid. Requests into the UN loss and damage fund already amount to $2.8bn, nearly eight times what is available, and that was before the Nepal disaster. According to the Lowy Institute, a thinktank, eight members of the UN’s Fund for responding to Loss and Damage that represent Africa, Asia and the least developed countries have called for an extraordinary meeting to discuss Nepal’s appeal, seeing it as “a test of whether the fund can act fast when it matters”.

In a 2025 book I co-authored with the UN’s Climate Vulnerability Forum and the V20 group of climate-vulnerable nations, we argued that loss and damage should be the third pillar of UN global climate diplomacy, alongside mitigation and adaptation. Seasoned Cop negotiators and UN observers acknowledged the scale of compensation is still hotly debated, and the “R” word, reparation, fiercely resisted. Meanwhile, an economist at the Maldives Finance Ministry told me that accessing any climate financing—including the UN loss and damage fund—was almost impossible.

That remains the case. The climate, however, continues to change: temperatures are rising and climate hazards are worsening. Nepal’s flood underscores this, for while the region is well known for flash floods and landfalls, no one had ever seen anything like this before. A senior UN source, who has witnessed many disasters, tells me he is “still having nightmares” from the videos. He also now expects loss and damage to shoot up the agenda at Cop31 in Turkey in November.

At the May 2025 ceremony for Nepal’s dying Yala glacier, which was conducted close to the site of this year’s disaster, a commemorative stone was erected. On it is an inscription by Icelandic author Andri Snaer Magnason. It reads: “A message to the future: Yala glacier is one of 54,000 glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalayas, most of which are expected to vanish this century due to global warming. This monument is to acknowledge that we know what is happening and what needs to be done. Only you know if we did it.”

नेपाली टाइम्स केरऽ एगो संपादकीय म॑ नोट करलऽ गेलऽ छै कि देश केरऽ नीति निर्माता सिनी क॑ चेतावनी देलऽ गेलऽ छेलै कि “अत्यधिक मौसम, हिमनदी झीलऽ म॑ फटै वाला बाढ़, आरू सीमा पार स॑ जलवायु आपदा स॑ पैदा होय वाला बाढ़ के तैयारी करलऽ जाय” ।

ओहि मे कहल गेल अछि जे इ कोनो ‘प्राकृतिक’ आपदा नहि छल। “एहि मे कोनो बात प्राकृतिक नहि छल-जीवाश्म ईंधन जरेबाक कारण ग्रीनहाउस गैस जमा होयबाक कारण ग्लेशियरक पिघलब नहि, ट्रांस-हिमालय नदी पर महग जलविद्युत संयंत्रक स्थान नहि, नदीक पाछाँ चलय लेल राजमार्गक डिजाइन नहि, ओकर आसपास बढ़ल बस्ती नहि, भ्रष्टाचार आ लोभ नहि, खराब शासन नहि।” संक्षेप मे ई एकटा पूर्वानुमानित त्रासदी छल।

शायद पूर्वानुमानित रूप स सेहो नेपाल आपदा स “हानि आ नुकसान” फंडिंग पर बहस फेर स सामने आबि गेल अछि। जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ सबसें अधिक कमजोर देशऽ क॑ मुआवजा दै वाला बड़ऽ उत्सर्जकऽ के अवधारणा २०२२ म॑ मिस्र म॑ आयोजित Cop27 जलवायु सम्मेलन म॑ सामने आरू केंद्र म॑ रहलऽ छेलै-जहाँ आपदा स॑ प्रभावित लोगऽ के मदद लेली एगो विशिष्ट कोष के स्थापना करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै-लेकिन ओकरऽ बाद स॑ ई पक्ष स॑ बाहर होय गेलऽ छै । सालाना 100 अरब-580 अरब डॉलर केरऽ कहलऽ गेलऽ जरूरत के तुलना म॑ ई पूरा कोष 631 मिलियन डॉलर प॑ बैठलऽ छै-जेकरा तरफ यूके (पांचमऽ सबसें बड़ऽ ऐतिहासिक कार्बन उत्सर्जक) न॑ 50 मिलियन डॉलर के योगदान देल॑ छै-जइ म॑ क्षतिपूर्ति लेली मात्र लगभग 350 मिलियन डॉलर उपलब्ध छै, आरू बाकी फंड चलाबै के लागत के तरफ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

2025 म॑ विदेशी सहायता लेली धन म॑ भी कटौती करला के साथ-साथ-जइ म॑ आपदा प्रतिक्रिया टीम भी शामिल छेलै जे एक समय म॑ नेपाल म॑ राहत प्रयासऽ म॑ सहयोग करी सकै छेलै-अमेरिका नुकसान आरू क्षति कोष समझौता स॑ पूरा तरह स॑ हटी गेलै । ब्रिटेन सहित अन्य धनी राष्ट्र सब सेहो अपन अंतरराष्ट्रीय विकास सहायता दायित्व मे कटौती केलक अछि।

बाढ़ि के बाद नेपाल के विदेश मंत्री शिसिर खनाल कान्तिपुर टीवी के कहलनि जे, नेपाल के अपन ग्रीनहाउस-गैस उत्सर्जन के देखैत “व्यावहारिक रूप सं नगण्य” अछि, देश भविष्य में सहायता के बात करय पर कम, आ “न्याय आ मुआवजा” पर बेसी ध्यान देत. मंत्री कहलनि जे, ई कोनो दान के बात नहि अछि, ई कानूनी आ नैतिक दायित्व के बात अछि, प्रमुख औद्योगिक उत्सर्जन करय वाला देश-जेना चीन, जे दुनिया के सबस बेसी उत्सर्जक अछि, अमेरिका के नंबर दू अछि, आ भारत के नंबर तीन पर अछि-नेपाल सन कमजोर राष्ट्र के मुआवजा देबय के ऐतिहासिक जिम्मेदारी अछि।”

नेपाल नदी सब पार जलविद्युत बांध बनेबा मे 6.7 अरब पाउंड स बेसी क निवेश केने छल, मुदा अगस्त क आपदा स 12 जलविद्युत संयंत्र समतल भ गेल, जाहि स देश क कुल ऊर्जा उत्पादन क्षमता क 10 प्रतिशत समाप्त भ गेल। 20 हजार स बेसी घर कए फेर स बनाबय पड़त। काठमांडू के सरकार के तरफ सं वसूली के लागत 5 अरब डॉलर सं बेसी के अनुमान अछि जे सकल घरेलू उत्पाद के लगभग 10 प्रतिशत अछि. एहि लागत कए पूरा करबा लेल नेपाल कए एखनो पारंपरिक सहायता क जरूरत अछि-खानाल ओहि आंकड़ा कए अपेक्षाकृत मामूली 20 मिलियन डॉलर रखने छथि।

सुनील आचार्य न॑ गार्जियन म॑ लिखलकै कि “हानि आरू नुकसान केरऽ वित्त क॑... मौजूदा आधिकारिक विकास सहायता के अतिरिक्त होना चाहियऽ” । हम इहो जोड़ब जे एकरा सेहो सहायता स कहीं बेसी आंकड़ा तक पहुंचय पड़त। संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ नुकसान आरू क्षति कोष म॑ आग्रह पहल॑ स॑ ही २.८ अरब डॉलर छै, जे उपलब्ध स॑ लगभग आठ गुना छै आरू ई नेपाल आपदा स॑ पहल॑ के छेलै । एकटा थिंकटैंक लोवी इंस्टीट्यूट के अनुसार अफ्रीका, एशिया आरू कम विकसित देशऽ के प्रतिनिधित्व करै वाला हानि आरू नुकसान के जवाब दै लेली संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ कोष केरऽ आठ सदस्य न॑ नेपाल केरऽ अपील प॑ चर्चा लेली एगो असाधारण बैठक के आह्वान करल॑ छै, जेकरा म॑ ई बात के “एक परीक्षण छै कि कोष जब॑ मायने रखै छै त॑ तेजी स॑ काम करी सकै छै कि नै” ।

2025 केरऽ एगो पुस्तक म॑ जेकरा म॑ हम्में संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ जलवायु भेद्यता मंच आरू जलवायु-असुरक्षित राष्ट्रऽ के वी-20 समूह के साथ सह-लेखन करलऽ छेलियै, हम्मं॑ ई तर्क देल॑ छेलियै कि नुकसान आरू नुकसान संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ वैश्विक जलवायु कूटनीति केरऽ तेसरऽ स्तंभ होना चाहियऽ, साथ ही साथ शमन आरू अनुकूलन भी । अनुभवी पुलिस वार्ताकार आरू संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ पर्यवेक्षक न॑ स्वीकार करलकै कि मुआवजा केरऽ पैमाना प॑ अखनी भी गरम बहस होय रहलऽ छै, आरू “आर” शब्द, मुआवजा केरऽ कड़ा विरोध करलऽ गेलै । एम्हर मालदीव वित्त मंत्रालयक एकटा अर्थशास्त्री हमरा कहलनि जे कोनो जलवायु वित्तपोषण - जाहि में संयुक्त राष्ट्रक नुकसान आ क्षति कोष सेहो शामिल अछि - तक पहुंच लगभग असंभव अछि.

से तऽ रहि गेल अछि। जलवायु में, लेकिन, परिवर्तन जारी छै: तापमान बढ़ी रहलऽ छै आरू जलवायु केरऽ खतरा बढ़ी रहलऽ छै । नेपाल के बाढ़ि एहि बात के रेखांकित करैत अछि, कारण ई क्षेत्र जखन कि फ्लैश फ्लड आ लैंडफॉल के लेल जानल जाइत अछि, एहि तरहक चीज पहिने कियो नहि देखने छल. संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ एगो वरिष्ठ सूत्र, जे बहुत आपदा के गवाह बनलऽ छै, हमरा बताबै छै कि ओकरा वीडियो स॑ “अखनी भी बुरा सपना आबी रहलऽ छै” । हुनका अब॑ ई भी उम्मीद छै कि नवंबर म॑ तुर्की म॑ Cop31 म॑ नुकसान आरू नुकसान के एजेंडा म॑ गोलीबारी होय जैतै ।

नेपाल केरऽ मरतऽ यला ग्लेशियर केरऽ मई २०२५ म॑ आयोजित समारोह म॑, जे ई साल केरऽ आपदा स्थल के नजदीक आयोजित करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, एक स्मारक पत्थर खड़ा करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । एकरा पर आइसलैंड केरऽ लेखक आंद्रे स्नायर मैग्नासन केरऽ शिलालेख छै । ओहि मे लिखल अछि: "भविष्य के लेल एकटा संदेश: यला ग्लेशियर हिन्दू कुश हिमालय के 54,000 ग्लेशियर मे सं एक अछि, जाहि मे सं अधिकांश ग्लेशियर एहि शताब्दी मे ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के कारण गायब भ जेबाक उम्मीद अछि. ई स्मारक एहि बात के स्वीकार करय लेल अछि जे हमरा सभ के पता अछि जे की भ रहल अछि आओर की करय के जरूरत अछि. केवल अहां सभ के पता अछि जे हम सभ ई काज केलहुं कि नहि."

description: Roma to support Nepal flood victims through Champions League match shirt  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
Italian football club AS Roma will help create awareness and raise funds for flood-affected people in Nepal by wearing shirts carrying a message of support during their UEFA Champions League match against Fenerbahce.

The Rome-based club, who travel to Istanbul for their opening match of Europe’s elite football competition on Thursday, will sport shirts emblazoned with the words “Together for Nepal” and the World Food Programme’s (WFP) logo after being banned from displaying their betting company sponsor in Turkiye.

The club will also raise funds for relief efforts by auctioning the special shirts and contributing the money to the WFP, the United Nations’ agency based in Rome.

More than 1,300 people have been confirmed dead and 5,000 remain missing after last month’s catastrophic floods.

Scientists say they were caused by the effects of climate change and triggered when part of a mountain glacier collapsed, sending a torrent of water and mud flooding down into Nepal’s Rasuwa and Nuwakot regions, as well as into China’s Tibet region.

“AS Roma and the WFP are joining forces to support the people of Nepal, who have been severely affected by the floods and landslides impacting the country,” Roma, one of the giants of Italian and European football, said in a statement on its website.

“The Giallorossi players will take the field with the World Food Programme logo on the front of their shirts, bringing attention to the emergency and raising visibility for WFP’s work in support of affected communities,” it added.

Advertisement

The move comes after Roma were prohibited from displaying the logo of their shirt sponsor, as the logos and names of sports betting or gambling companies are banned on team kits in Turkiye.

Champions League honours Nepal flood victims

A moment of silence for Nepal’s flood victims was observed across all Champions League matches as the competition kicked off its new season on Tuesday. Matches held on Wednesday followed suit, with players, coaching staff, officials and fans honouring the victims before kickoff in all fixtures.

Screens in all stadiums displayed messages in support of the flood affectees.

English Premier League club Arsenal have also contributed to flood relief efforts via the Arsenal Foundation and its charity partner, Save the Children, which is responding in Nepal.

चैम्पियंस लीग नेपाल बाढि पीडित के सम्मानित

मंगलदिन सं प्रतियोगिता के नवका सीजन शुरू भेला पर नेपाल के बाढ़ि पीड़ित के लेल चैंपियंस लीग के सभ मैच मे मौन के क्षण देखल गेल. बुधवार क॑ आयोजित मैचऽ म॑ भी एकरऽ अनुसरण करलऽ गेलै, जेकरा म॑ खिलाड़ी, कोचिंग स्टाफ, अधिकारी आरू प्रशंसक सब फिक्सर म॑ किकऑफ स॑ पहल॑ पीड़ितऽ क॑ सम्मानित करलकै ।

सब स्टेडियम के स्क्रीन पर बाढ़ि प्रभावित के समर्थन में संदेश देखाओल गेल छल.

इंग्लिश प्रीमियर लीग क्लब आर्सनल न॑ भी आर्सनल फाउंडेशन आरू ओकरऽ चैरिटी पार्टनर सेव द चिल्ड्रेन के माध्यम स॑ बाढ़ राहत के प्रयास म॑ योगदान देल॑ छै, जे नेपाल म॑ एकरऽ जवाब द॑ रहलऽ छै ।

title: Helping the most vulnerable in Nepal - BMA
description: Helping the most vulnerable in Nepal  BMA
publisher.title: BMA
full_article:
The humanitarian response to the flash flood disaster in Nepal has saved hundreds of lives. Co-ordinated rescue teams and doctors have picked up people and delivered them to nearby hospitals.

The disaster struck on the morning of 26 August, sweeping away settlements beside the Trishuli River for up to 72km downstream.

An MSF ( Médecins sans Frontières) emergency team arrived in Nepal following the flood. According to reports, at least 1,000 people have been killed, with more than 3,900 still missing.

After assessing the situation, MSF decided not to launch a humanitarian response, saying: ‘ Our expertise does not lie in the recovery, rehabilitation, and reconstruction activities that people in Nepal now need. We extend our admiration and respect to local communities, the Nepali authorities and all those responding tirelessly under difficult conditions, helping people recover from this disaster.’

The Nepalese people told the MSF that their biggest needs now are for recovery – for roads and markets to reopen, for schools, homes and infrastructure to be rebuilt. MSF says it is clear that continued, significant, relief efforts and funding for people in affected communities is required now and in the weeks and months to come.

Women and children have been particularly badly affected by the disaster, according to the UN, who launched a rescue effort immediately after it unfolded.

It says 43,000 women and girls now need humanitarian assistance, and that food and water are running out and protection risks are growing. Pregnant women and girls were washed away simply because they could not reach higher ground quickly enough, the UN told the press.

Access to healthcare has become a huge issue according to the World Health Organization. A spokesperson for the who said health facilities have been damaged while others cannot be reached, meaning ‘people on the ground don't have a health facility available at the time of their biggest needs’.

He added that, ‘while immediate efforts remain focused on life-saving interventions … preventing secondary public health impacts is equally important’.

The BMA has offered its support for those affected. It says: ‘We are deeply saddened by the devastating flash floods that struck the Nepal-Tibet border region that has claimed hundreds of lives with many more still missing.

‘Our thoughts are with everyone affected, including those across the UK who may have family, friends, and colleagues in the region and to those who may be personally affected by the disaster's toll. This disaster is also a stark reminder of how a warming climate is increasing the risk of such catastrophic events for vulnerable communities worldwide – a trend with growing implications for global health.

‘We know that many NHS staff have close ties to Nepal and the wider region, and that news of an event on this scale can weigh heavily, even from a distance. We want any of our members grappling with this to know that support is available, whether through their employer's occupational health services, the NHS's staff support lines, or through the BMA's own wellbeing services and counselling support for members.’

It also points out it stands shoulder to shoulder with ‘the Nepal Medical Association and recognises the extraordinary humanitarian response already under way, and the healthcare professionals — in Nepal, Tibet, and further afield — working under immense pressure to treat the injured and search for the missing. Their dedication reflects the very best of our profession’. Some of the BMA's international advocacy efforts have centred around asking the UK Government to take more ambitious climate action. This includes securing a multi-year commitment to International Climate Finance to support preparedness and response, including climate adaptation and mitigation efforts, as well as the Loss and Damage Fund for countries experiencing harmful climatic events. These harms are felt most acutely by populations that are often least responsible for the emissions driving the climate crisis but disproportionately affected by its consequences. It has been widely reported that the flash flood is linked to climate change.

Speaking to The Guardian newspaper, Nepali prime minister Balendra Shah said the catastrophe was ‘not an ordinary’ event.

Mr Shah said on social media that ‘the risks we face in the Himalayan region are increasing alongside climate change … It is now time for us to strongly raise with the international community the issue of the disasters we are experiencing as a result of climate change’.

Addressing the house of representative of the Federal Parliament of Nepal, Mr Shah said: ‘This incident shows the increasing risk the people of the mountain region have to bear with the occurrence of climate change … There is a global contribution behind climate change. And the responsibility to manage and minimise its effects also rests on the global community.’

Chris Patterson is production editor of The Doctor

नेपालमे भेल आकस्मिक बाढ़िक आपदामे मानवीय प्रतिक्रियासँ सैकड़ो लोकक जान बँचल अछि । समन्वित बचाव दल आ डॉक्टर लोक के उठा क पास के अस्पताल पहुंचा देलक अछि।

26 अगस्त क भोर मे आयल इ आपदा त्रिशुली नदी क कात मे 72 किलोमीटर तक नीचा बस्ती कए बहरा गेल।

बाढ़ि के बाद एमएसएफ ( Médecins sans Frontières) के आपातकालीन टीम नेपाल पहुंचल अछि. खबर के अनुसार कम सं कम एक हजार लोक के मौत भ चुकल अछि, जखन कि 3900 सं बेसि लोक एखनो लापता अछि.

स्थिति के आकलन करला के बाद एमएसएफ मानवीय प्रतिक्रिया नै शुरू करै के फैसला करलकै आरू कहलकै कि ‘ हमरऽ विशेषज्ञता वसूली, पुनर्वास, आरू पुनर्निर्माण के गतिविधि म॑ नै छै जेकरऽ जरूरत नेपाल के लोगऽ क॑ अब॑ छै । हम स्थानीय समुदाय, नेपाली प्राधिकारी आ कठिन परिस्थिति मे अथक प्रतिक्रिया देबय वाला सब गोटे के अपन प्रशंसा आ सम्मान दैत छी, जे लोक के एहि आपदा सं उबरय मे मदद करैत छी.'

नेपाली जनता एमएसएफ के कहलक जे आब हुनकर सबस पैघ जरूरत अछि रिकवरी के – सड़क आ बाजार के फेर सं खुलय के, स्कूल, घर आओर बुनियादी ढांचा के पुनर्निर्माण के. एमएसएफ के कहना छै कि ई साफ छै कि प्रभावित समुदायऽ के लोगऽ लेली लगातार, महत्वपूर्ण, राहत प्रयास आरू फंडिंग के जरूरत छै अखनी आरू आबै वाला हफ्ता आरू महीना म॑ ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ अनुसार ई आपदा स॑ महिला आरू बच्चा खास करी क॑ बहुत प्रभावित होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा न॑ एकरऽ खुलासा के तुरंत बाद बचाव के प्रयास शुरू करी देलकै ।

एकरऽ कहना छै कि अब॑ ४३,००० महिला आरू लड़की सिनी क॑ मानवीय सहायता के जरूरत छै, आरू भोजन आरू पानी खतम होय रहलऽ छै आरू सुरक्षा के खतरा बढ़ी रहलऽ छै । संयुक्त राष्ट्र न॑ प्रेस क॑ बतैलकै कि गर्भवती महिला आरू लड़की सिनी क॑ खाली ऐसनऽ वजह स॑ बहाय देलऽ गेलै कि वू काफी जल्दी ऊँचऽ जगह प॑ नै पहुँची सकलै ।

विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन के अनुसार स्वास्थ्य सेवा के पहुंच एकटा पैघ मुद्दा बनि गेल अछि. केरऽ प्रवक्ता न॑ कहलकै कि स्वास्थ्य सुविधा क॑ नुकसान पहुँचलऽ छै जबकि दोसरऽ स॑ संपर्क नै करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै, मतलब कि ‘जमीन प॑ मौजूद लोगऽ के पास अपनऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ जरूरत के समय स्वास्थ्य सुविधा उपलब्ध नै छै’ ।

हुनी आरू कहलकै कि, ‘जबकि तत्काल प्रयास जीवन रक्षक हस्तक्षेप प केंद्रित छै ... माध्यमिक जनस्वास्थ्य प्रभाव क रोकना भी ओतने महत्वपूर्ण छै’ ।

बीएमए प्रभावित लोक के लेल अपन सहयोग के पेशकश केलक अछि. ओहि मे कहल गेल अछि : ‘नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा क्षेत्र मे आयल विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ि सँ हमरा लोकनि गहींर दुखी छी जाहि मे सैकड़ों लोकक जान गेल अछि आ कतेको लोक एखनो लापता अछि ।

‘हमरऽ विचार सब प्रभावित लोगऽ के साथ छै, जेकरा म॑ पूरा यूके म॑ भी शामिल छै, जेकरऽ परिवार, दोस्त, आरू सहयोगी क्षेत्र म॑ हो सकै छै आरू वू लोगऽ के साथ छै जे आपदा केरऽ टोल स॑ व्यक्तिगत रूप स॑ प्रभावित होय सकै छै । ई आपदा ई बात केरऽ सख्त याद दिलाबै छै कि कोना गर्मी बढ़ै वाला जलवायु दुनिया भर म॑ कमजोर समुदायऽ लेली ऐसनऽ विनाशकारी घटना के खतरा बढ़ा रहलऽ छै – जेकरऽ प्रवृत्ति वैश्विक स्वास्थ्य प॑ बढ़त॑ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

‘हमरा सब क॑ पता छै कि एनएचएस केरऽ बहुत कर्मचारी केरऽ नेपाल आरू व्यापक क्षेत्र स॑ घनिष्ठ संबंध छै, आरू ई पैमाना प॑ कोनो आयोजन के खबर दूर स॑ भी भारी पड़॑ सकै छै । हम चाहय छी जे अइ सं जूझय वाला हमर कोनों सदस्य इ जानय कि सहायता उपलब्ध छै, चाहे ओ ओकर नियोक्ता कें व्यावसायिक स्वास्थ्य सेवाक कें माध्यम सं हो, एनएचएस कें कर्मचारी सहायता लाइनक कें माध्यम सं हो, या बीएमए कें अपन कल्याण सेवाक आ सदस्यक कें लेल परामर्श सहायता कें माध्यम सं.’

ई भी इशारा करै छै कि ई ‘नेपाल मेडिकल एसोसिएशन के साथ कंधा स॑ कंधा मिला क॑ खड़ा छै आरू पहल॑ स॑ ही चलै वाला असाधारण मानवीय प्रतिक्रिया क॑ पहचानै छै, आरू स्वास्थ्य सेवा पेशेवरऽ — नेपाल, तिब्बत, आरू आरू दूर-दूरऽ म॑ — घायलऽ के इलाज आरू लापता लोगऽ के खोज लेली अपार दबाव म॑ काम करी रहलऽ छै । हुनकऽ समर्पण हमरऽ पेशे केरऽ बहुत बेहतरीन बात क॑ दर्शाबै छै’ । बीएमए केरऽ कुछ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय वकालत केरऽ प्रयास यूके सरकार स॑ जलवायु के बारे म॑ आरू महत्वाकांक्षी कार्रवाई करै लेली कहै के इर्द-गिर्द केंद्रित छै । एहि मे जलवायु अनुकूलन आ शमन प्रयासक कें संग-संग हानिकारक जलवायु घटनाक कें अनुभव करय वाला देशक कें लेल नुकसान आ क्षति कोष सहित तैयारी आ प्रतिक्रिया कें समर्थन कें लेल अंतर्राष्ट्रीय जलवायु वित्त कें लेल बहुवर्षीय प्रतिबद्धता सुरक्षित करनाय शामिल छै. इ नुकसान सब सं बेसि ओ आबादी कें द्वारा महसूस कैल जायत छै जे अक्सर जलवायु संकट कें बढ़ावा देवय वाला उत्सर्जन कें लेल कम जिम्मेदार होयत छै मुदा ओकर परिणाम सं असमान रूप सं प्रभावित होयत छै. व्यापक रूप स॑ ई बात के खबर आबी रहलऽ छै कि ई फ्लैश फ्लड जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ जुड़लऽ छै ।

द गार्जियन अखबार सँ बातचीत करैत नेपाली प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह प्रलय ‘साधारण’ घटना नहि रहल बतौलनि ।

श्री शाह न॑ सोशल मीडिया प॑ कहलकै कि ‘जलवायु परिवर्तन के साथ-साथ हिमालयन क्षेत्र म॑ हमरा सब क॑ जे जोखिम के सामना करना पड़॑ छै, वू बढ़ी रहलऽ छै ... अब॑ समय आबी गेलऽ छै कि हम्मं॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय के साथ जलवायु परिवर्तन के परिणामस्वरूप हम्मं॑ जे आपदा के सामना करी रहलऽ छियै ओकरऽ मुद्दा क॑ मजबूती स॑ उठाबै’ ।

नेपाल के संघीय संसद के प्रतिनिधि सभा के संबोधित करैत श्री शाह कहलनि जे, ‘ई घटना जलवायु परिवर्तन के घटना सं पहाड़ी क्षेत्र के लोक के बढ़ैत जोखिम के दर्शाबैत अछि ... जलवायु परिवर्तन के पाछु वैश्विक योगदान अछि। आरू एकरऽ प्रभाव क॑ प्रबंधित करै आरू कम स॑ कम करै के जिम्मेदारी भी वैश्विक समुदाय प॑ छै ।’

title: Nepal floods death toll climbs to 1,377; search operations continue for more than 5,000 missing - The Hindu
description: Nepal floods death toll climbs to 1,377; search operations continue for more than 5,000 missing  The Hindu
publisher.title: The Hindu
full_article:
The death toll due to the flash floods in Nepal rose to 1,377 on Thursday (September 10, 2026) as more bodies were recovered from the affected districts, while rescue and search operations continue for more than 5,000 missing people, authorities said.

At least 364 bodies have been recovered from Chitwan district, 228 from Nawalparasi East, 222 from Nawalparasi West and 198 from Nuwakot, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).

Nepal flash floods wash away illusions of clean, easy hydropower

Similarly, 178 bodies have been recovered from Rasuwa, 77 from Gorkha, 70 from Dhading and 38 from Tanahu, it said.

Two flood victims died during treatment in Kathmandu.

The joint command of security personnel has continued search and rescue operations for the missing people, estimated to be 5,130.

Also Read: Nepal flash floods: What caused the devastation?

So far, 13,656 people have been rescued from the flood-affected areas.

The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal.

ALSO WATCH Watch: What is driving disasters in the Himalayas? C.P. Rajendran explains

The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.

The disaster also killed at least 43 people on the Chinese side, while more than 500 people remain missing in Tibet, according to Chinese media reports.

SOUTHFIELD, Mich., Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Helping Hand for Relief and Development (HHRD) has launched a $250,000 emergency appeal to provide critical humanitarian assistance to families affected by the catastrophic floods that struck Nepal on August 26.

HHRD is Raising Funds for Nepal Flood Relief

The disaster began when a glacier collapse in the Himalayas triggered a massive surge of water, ice, rock and mud through the Trishuli River system, devastating communities along Nepal's northern border with Tibet. The floods have caused widespread loss of life and left thousands missing, while destroying homes, roads, bridges, and critical infrastructure. Current estimates indicate that the disaster has caused approximately $2.56 billion in damage, with thousands of families displaced and communities struggling to access necessities.

Urgent Needs on the Ground

As search and rescue operations continue, affected families urgently need food, clean drinking water, emergency shelter, hygiene supplies, medical assistance and other essential relief items. Damaged roads and bridges have made reaching many communities difficult, further increasing the urgency of the response. Nepalese authorities have mobilized thousands of security personnel and helicopters for rescue and relief operations, while specialized international assistance has also been brought in to support difficult rescue efforts.

HHRD has been serving vulnerable communities in Nepal since 2015, with ongoing programs supporting orphans, water access, livelihoods, healthcare and seasonal relief. Through its established presence in the country, HHRD is mobilizing resources for this emergency response and working to deliver essential assistance to families affected by the floods.

HHRD is calling on donors, supporters and communities across the United States to help raise $250,000 for Nepal flood relief. Every contribution can help provide families with the essentials they need to survive the immediate crisis and begin rebuilding their lives.

Donate today and help HHRD reach families in Nepal when they need it most.

साउथफील्ड, मिशिगन, १० सितम्बर २०२६ /पीआरन्यूजवायर/ -- हेल्पिंग हैंड फॉर रिलीफ एंड डेवलपमेंट (एचएचआरडी) न॑ २६ अगस्त क॑ नेपाल म॑ आबी गेलऽ विनाशकारी बाढ़ स॑ प्रभावित परिवारऽ क॑ महत्वपूर्ण मानवीय सहायता प्रदान करै लेली २५०,००० डॉलर के आपातकालीन अपील शुरू करलकै ।

एचएचआरडी नेपाल बाढ़ राहतके लेल धन जुटा रहल अछि

आपदा तखन शुरू भेल जखन हिमालय में ग्लेशियर के गिरला सं त्रिशूली नदी प्रणाली के माध्यम सं पानि, बर्फ, चट्टान आ थाल के भारी उफान शुरू भ गेल, जे नेपाल के तिब्बत सं उत्तरी सीमा पर समुदाय के तबाह क देलक. बाढ़ि के कारण व्यापक जान-माल के नुकसान भेल अछि आ हजारों लोक लापता भ गेल अछि, जखन कि घर, सड़क, पुल, आ महत्वपूर्ण बुनियादी ढांचा तबाह भ गेल अछि. वर्तमान अनुमान संकेत करै छै कि ई आपदा स॑ लगभग २.५६ अरब डॉलर के नुकसान होय ​​गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ हजारों परिवार विस्थापित होय गेलऽ छै आरू समुदायऽ क॑ जरूरत के सामान तक पहुँचै म॑ परेशानी होय रहलऽ छै ।

जमीन पर तत्काल आवश्यकता

जेना-जेना खोज आ बचाव अभियान जारी छै, प्रभावित परिवारक कें भोजन, स्वच्छ पेयजल, आपातकालीन आश्रय, स्वच्छता कें सामान, चिकित्सा सहायता आ अन्य आवश्यक राहत वस्तुअक कें तत्काल जरूरत छै. क्षतिग्रस्त सड़क आ पुल के कारण बहुत समुदाय तक पहुंचनाय मुश्किल भ गेल अछि, जाहि सं प्रतिक्रिया के तात्कालिकता आओर बढ़ि गेल अछि. नेपाली प्राधिकारी हजारों सुरक्षाकर्मी आ हेलीकॉप्टर के बचाव आ राहत कार्य के लेल जुटान केने अछि, तहिना कठिन बचाव प्रयास के समर्थन के लेल विशेष अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सहायता सेहो आनल गेल अछि।

एचएचआरडी 2015 सं नेपाल मे कमजोर समुदायक कें सेवा द रहल छै, जइ मे अनाथ, जल पहुंच, आजीविका, स्वास्थ्य सेवा आ मौसमी राहत कें सहायता कें कार्यक्रम जारी छै. देश मे अपन स्थापित उपस्थिति कें माध्यम सं एचएचआरडी अइ आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया कें लेल संसाधन जुटा रहल छै आ बाढ़ सं प्रभावित परिवारक कें आवश्यक सहायता पहुंचाबय कें काज कयर रहल छै.

एचएचआरडी पूरा अमेरिका मे दाता, समर्थक आ समुदाय स आह्वान क रहल अछि जे नेपाल बाढ़ि राहत लेल अढ़ाई लाख डॉलर जुटेबा मे मदद करथि। हर योगदान परिवारक कें तत्काल संकट सं बचय आ ओकर जीवन कें पुनर्निर्माण शुरू करय कें लेल आवश्यक आवश्यक वस्तुअक उपलब्ध करावा मे मदद कयर सकय छै.

full_article:
(Photo: X)

Many Christians are among those killed and still missing as a result of the devastating flood that hit Nepal at the end of August. So far over 900 people are confirmed dead while more than 4,400 are still missing.

Christians, though a small minority in the country, have also been impacted, with dozens killed and many believers and pastors missing, as well as whole churches swept away in the deluge.

One on the ground partner of International Christian Concern said, “Local church leaders are facing severe communication challenges. Electricity, mobile networks, internet connectivity, and road access have been disrupted, making it extremely difficult to gather accurate information.

“It may take several more days to assess the full extent of damage and loss. We as a ministry are keeping a close eye on the situation, looking to assist and bring emergency relief to families affected by the floods.”

According to Nepali Christian Churches UK, churches in Rasuwa and Nuwakot have been hit particularly hard. Leaving aside the damage to the buildings, large portions of the congregations remain unaccounted for.

Christianity in Nepal remains a tiny minority, at around 1.8 per cent of the population. Christian leaders in the country have suggested that, much like in India, the authorities and society at large have taken efforts to act against the faith, which they see as an assault on the nation’s Hindu identity.

Pastors have been arrested, churches attacked and Indian-style anti-conversion laws passed. Attempts have also been made by Hindus to have the country declared an officially Hindu nation.

Despite this, Christianity in Nepal is growing. That 1.8 per cent represents over half a million believers as of the 2021 census. Ten years previously the raw number of Christians in the country was just 375,000 (representing 1.4 per cent of the overall population). The growth is largely due to conversions rather than a higher-than-average birthrate.

अगस्त के अंत में नेपाल में आयल विनाशकारी बाढ़ के परिणामस्वरूप मारल गेल आ एखनो लापता लोक में बहुत ईसाई सेहो शामिल अछि। एखन धरि 900 सं बेसि लोक के मौत के पुष्टि भ चुकल अछि जखन कि 4400 सं बेसि लोक अखनो लापता अछि.

ईसाई, भले ही देश केरऽ छोटऽ अल्पसंख्यक छै, लेकिन एकरऽ असर भी पड़लऽ छै, दर्जनों लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै आरू बहुत सारा विश्वासी आरू पादरी लापता होय गेलऽ छै, साथ ही साथ पूरा चर्च भी बाढ़ म॑ बह॑ गेलऽ छै ।

इंटरनेशनल क्रिश्चियन कन्सर्न केरऽ एगो ग्राउंड पार्टनर न॑ कहलकै, “स्थानीय चर्च केरऽ नेता सिनी क॑ गंभीर संचार चुनौती के सामना करना पड़॑ छै ।बिजली, मोबाइल नेटवर्क, इंटरनेट कनेक्टिविटी, आरू सड़कऽ के पहुँच बाधित होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ सही जानकारी जुटाना अत्यंत मुश्किल होय गेलऽ छै ।

ओ कहला जे नुकसान आ नुकसान क पूरा सीमा क आकलन करबा मे कई दिन आओर लागि सकैत अछि। हम एकटा मंत्रालय के रूप में स्थिति पर पूरा नजर राखि रहल छी, बाढ़ि सं प्रभावित परिवार के मदद आ आपातकालीन राहत देबय के कोशिश क रहल छी।”

नेपाली क्रिश्चियन चर्च यूकेके अनुसार रसुवा आ नुवाकोटके चर्चसबके विशेष प्रहार भेल अछि । भवन सब के नुकसान के छोड़ि दी त मंडली के पैघ हिस्सा के हिसाब नहिं अछि.

नेपाल मे ईसाई धर्म एकटा छोट अल्पसंख्यक बनल अछि, जेकर आबादी लगभग 1.8 प्रतिशत अछि । देश केरऽ ईसाई नेता सिनी न॑ सुझाव देल॑ छै कि भारत के तरह ही अधिकारियऽ आरू समाज न॑ भी ई आस्था के खिलाफ काम करै के कोशिश करलकै, जेकरा वू राष्ट्र केरऽ हिन्दू पहचान प॑ हमला के रूप म॑ देखै छै ।

पास्टर सब के गिरफ्तार कायल गेल अछि, चर्च पर हमला भ गेल अछि आ भारतीय शैली के धर्म परिवर्तन विरोधी कानून पास भ गेल अछि। हिन्दू लोकनि द्वारा सेहो एहि देश केँ आधिकारिक तौर पर हिन्दू राष्ट्र घोषित करबाक प्रयास कयल गेल अछि ।

एकर बादो नेपाल मे ईसाई धर्म बढ़ि रहल अछि । ओ 1.8 प्रतिशत 2021 के जनगणना के अनुसार डेढ़ लाख सं बेसी आस्तिक के प्रतिनिधित्व करैत अछि. दस साल पहिने देश में ईसाई के कच्चा संख्या महज 375,000 (समग्र आबादी के 1.4 प्रतिशत के प्रतिनिधित्व करैत अछि) छल. ई वृद्धि केरऽ बहुत हद तक औसत स॑ अधिक जन्म दर के बजाय रूपांतरण के कारण छै ।

title: N.C. South Asian communities rally behind those affected by Nepal flood - The Daily Tar Heel
description: N.C. South Asian communities rally behind those affected by Nepal flood  The Daily Tar Heel
publisher.title: The Daily Tar Heel
full_article:
At 8:37 a.m. on Aug. 26, a massive glacier sheared off a Himalayan peak in Nepal’s Langtang National Park near the Nepal-Tibet border, and the subsequent landslide sent a barrage of ice and debris crashing down into the Trishuli River and Bhote Koshi River valleys. In less than 10 minutes, a wall of floodwater rushed toward the border at Gyirong Port in a sheer force of destruction, turning a once-lively immigration center into a barren, gray mud field.

CCTV footage of the moment the flood hit as people scattered to escape the torrential wave went viral, becoming the way many people all over the world learned of the tragedy. The world watched their screens in horror as people were drowned and buried under mud and wreckage.

As of Tuesday, the Government of Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority reports that over 1,350 people are confirmed dead, and around 5,300 remain missing. Over 13,500 people have been rescued, and over 7,000 are injured and currently receiving treatment.

Almost 8,000 miles away, Nepali Americans in North Carolina are feeling the weight of this tragedy and are doing what they can to honor the victims and help from across the globe.

Last Wednesday, the Nepal Center of North Carolina organized a candlelight vigil at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, a Hindu temple in Morrisville. Various community leaders attended the vigil and shared sentiments honoring the victims of the flood and encouraging support for the state’s Nepali community.

Community members shared personal stories about friends and family members they had lost, and organizers from NCNC also shared information about fundraising initiatives.

Prachand Shrestha, who attended the vigil, said he learned of what had happened in his home country the same way that many others had: through social media.

Shrestha, who lives in Morrisville but is originally from Kathmandu, the capital city of Nepal, said he first heard the news when he saw the devastating footage circulating through Facebook. As he watched bridges and houses go down from thousands of miles away, he said his heart started to shake.

For Shrestha, news coverage in the U.S. of the destruction and loss of life is important to bring global attention to Nepal and Tibet, but he said it is also important to show the mental toll the tragedy has taken on the families of the victims so that the world can understand the unimaginable weight of such a tragedy.

“This kind of impact, or the calamities or casualties, are for everyone to consume,” Shrestha said. “When I say consume — to take it inside and introspect the level of calamity.”

Shrestha’s daughter, Avani Shrestha, is co-president of Dedicated to Our Community of North Carolina, a group of elementary, middle and high school students across North Carolina that volunteer and work to raise funds for various community issues. Avani Shrestha, her co-president Hansitha Teluguntla and youth ambassador Agrata Dahal shared DOC NC’s current fundraising initiatives at the vigil, encouraging attendees and community members to donate to the NCNC which will then donate the funds to the Nepali Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund.

“Even though we’re not there right now, what’s happening there still affects us in North Carolina,” Avani Shrestha said. “Just being aware of that and raising awareness about how these floods have devastated, for probably not only this year but for years later on, and it’s going to take a lot of time and money to rebuild.”

Teluguntla added that she has noticed that the news is largely spreading through word of mouth in the South Asian community, and it is important for people outside of that to speak out as well.

That word of mouth has been powerful in DOC NC’s fundraising efforts. Of their $10,000 goal, they have raised $8,000 and plan to raise more than their original goal if they can. The organization’s leaders said they started by sharing helpful links throughout their community. Now, many young volunteers and their families are selling handmade items such as hair accessories and candles to raise money.

Both Avani Shrestha and Teluguntla said that it is important for all people to help those who are affected by such tragedies as much as possible, even if they are not from the same country.

“You might not be Nepali, but you’re always surrounded by a community who’s somehow connected to them,” Avani Shrestha said. “So it’s more inspiring to donate and advocate for them because there’s been a lot of trouble in Nepal recently.”

Dahal added that there is no such thing as helping too little or too much, and doing what we can is more than enough.

“Especially in today’s society, today’s world, I think we could all use a little more love,” Dahal said. “So just the love and support that people have been sharing and are continuing to share truly will help strengthen Nepal, and Nepal will continue to be as resilient and beautiful as it is.”
